previewText: Reflect on what thrived in your Portland garden and discover tips for a strong start next season.

contentBlocks.tagline: Review, Reflect, and Rejoice in Your Garden’s Achievements!

contentBlocks.imageAlt: A lush garden with an array of colorful flowers.

contentBlocks.body:
As the year winds down, now’s a great time to take stock of your garden. Take a walk around and note which plants thrived, which areas brought you the most joy, and where you might want to try something new next year.

This week, clear out any spent annuals and tidy perennial beds. Compost healthy plant debris, but discard anything diseased to keep problems from carrying over. This is also a smart time to jot down which varieties performed best in your unique Portland microclimate.

contentBlocks.headline: Practical Tasks for Your Year-End Review
contentBlocks.body:
Cut back perennial stems like Black-Eyed Susan and hydrangea blooms once they’ve faded, but leave ornamental grasses for winter interest and wildlife shelter. If you grew Korean Spice Viburnum, check for any crossing branches or spent flower heads and trim lightly where needed.

Take a few photos of your favorite garden moments—they’ll be helpful as you plan next season’s plantings and layout.
contentBlocks.imageAlt: A garden vibrant with purple and white blossoms.
